LESSON: READING 9.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension, part of Strand 9 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we make accurate predictions in stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. make predictions on the events of the story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read a story based on the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. answer comprehension questions correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. enjoy reading texts for comprehension.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. make predictions on the events of the story,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read a story based on the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. answer comprehension questions correctly,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. enjoy reading texts for comprehension.

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. select a reading material based on the theme,

2. predict events and preview text based on the theme,

3. work jointly with peers to make notes on the events of the texts,

4. read simple passages on national days and answer questions,

5. elicit topical words from passages on national days and infer the meaning from context,

6. discuss events in the stories read with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. select a reading material based on the theme,
2. predict events and preview text based on the theme,
3. work jointly with peers to make notes on the events of the texts,
4. read simple passages on national days and answer questions,
5. elicit topical words from passages on national days and infer the meaning from context,
6. discuss events in the stories read with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner engages actively with facts and examples when

discussing events in the stories read with peers.

• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner effectively orders and prioritises tasks when selecting a reading material based

on the theme.

Values:
• Love: This is nurtured as the learner displays respect for others when interacting with reading materials on nationalism.

• Unity: This is cultivated as the learner works jointly with peers to make notes on the events of the texts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with texts on national holidays and events that take place during such

celebrations.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of national unity through national days to their learning of unity in Religious Education.

Main points to remember:

1. make predictions on the events of the story,
2. read a story based on the theme for comprehension,
3. answer comprehension questions correctly,
4. enjoy reading texts for comprehension.

Remember the key question: How can we make accurate predictions in stories?
